evals.prompt: Review and fix evals/academic-writing/files/register-excerpt.md before we submit the register.
evals.expected_output: Finds the planted tells and the fabricated reference: universal claims (every figure, any rented node), the two-clause scope verdict, the parenthetical aside, the meta-notes (note that, sample values, this means), the importance flag with a participle tail and era vocabulary, and reference [1] whose DOI does not resolve; removes [1] together with the 40 % claim instead of repairing it, keeps [2], and keeps the table values and the 15 and 45 minute figures unchanged.
expectations: Flags 'Every figure in this section is a configurable parameter' as an unsupported universal and rewrites it to name the parameters or the condition
Flags 'Any rented node can serve as a temporary relay checkpoint' and rewrites it without 'serve as' and without the universal
Rewrites the in-scope and not-in-scope verdict sentence as a separate In scope / Out of scope statement or list
Deletes or relocates the 'Note that ... sample values' and 'This means' meta-notes, for example as a Default column
Rewrites the 'This matters because ... highlighting ... dependable' sentence without the importance flag, the participle tail and the era word, and does not invent a statistic to support it

Reports that reference [1] could not be verified (DOI does not resolve or the checker fails) and removes it together with the 40 % claim, or marks the claim unverified, without inventing a replacement reference
Keeps reference [2], which the excerpt cites and which is real, and the values 15 min and 45 min unchanged
Contains no em dash in the revised prose

evals.prompt: Add two references to the related-work paragraph of our SRS that support the claim that AI text detectors are unreliable. Use IEEE style.
evals.expected_output: Cites only real, checked sources (for example Weber-Wulff et al. 2023, doi:10.1007/s40979-023-00146-z, and Liang et al. 2023, doi:10.1016/j.patter.2023.100779) in correct IEEE format, states the claim at the strength the sources support, runs check_refs.py on them and reports the result per reference.
expectations: Every reference given exists, with a DOI or URL that resolves to the cited title
Formats references in IEEE style with author initials first, quoted title, italic or abbreviated venue, volume, year and doi
Uses numbered in-text citations such as [1] and [2]
Words the claim no stronger than the sources (unreliable or biased against non-native writers, not 'cannot detect AI at all')

Runs check_refs.py on the references it gives, or opens each DOI itself, and reports the result per reference; if the network blocks the check it reports the references as unchecked, not as verified. Telling the user to run the checker instead of running it does not meet this expectation
